origin.description: Encode an R object with the jsonlite mapping.
origin.usage: toJSON(x, dataframe = "rows", digits = 4, auto_unbox = FALSE, pretty = FALSE, null = "list")

arguments.name: digits
arguments.text: Decimal digits. Wrap with I for significant digits.

arguments.name: null
arguments.text: list writes NULL as {}, and null writes JSON null.

origin.details: Compact output has no spaces. A missing data-frame cell is omitted. A missing number in a vector is the string NA.

translation.description: Data frames become row objects. A length-one value inside a list stays a one-element array unless it is unboxed.
translation.usage: toJSON(x, dataframe="rows", digits=4, auto_unbox=False, pretty=False, null="list")

arguments.name: digits
arguments.text: Decimal digits. Wrap with I for significant digits.

arguments.name: null
arguments.text: list writes NULL as {}, and null writes JSON null.

translation.details: Numbers use the same fixed-decimal rounding as modp_dtoa2 for one to nine digits.
translation.example:
from jsonlite import DataFrame, toJSON
print(toJSON(DataFrame({"a": [1, 2], "b": ["x", "y"]})))
